name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running for reelection with nearly $1M raised
Republican challenger Martha Fierro has shown no fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Garcia holds a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat, out-raised her opponent by a wide margin, and benefits from outside spending while facing none. With no polls or expert ratings, the fundamentals and market pricing both point to a comfortable incumbent win.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Garcia or a strong national Republican wave could narrow the margin, though a seat this blue is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks reelection in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She is a well-established incumbent who has raised nearly a million dollars and holds over $200,000 in cash, with outside groups adding more than $500,000 in support on her behalf. Her Republican opponent, Martha Fierro, has reported no fundraising and no outside backing.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with Garcia heavily favored to return to Congress.
